extracted.intended_audience: Users of the Singular computer-algebra system (mathematicians / researchers wanting to typeset algebraic objects, visualize surfaces, or compute with Brill–Noether / AG-code routines).
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation and usage requirements for several Singular libraries (latex.lib, surf.lib, surfex.lib, brnoeth.lib): global variables, procedures, their arguments, return values, assumptions, and examples for typesetting, plotting, and algebraic-geometry computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global LaTeX typesetting variables (latex.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: TeXwidth, TeXnofrac, TeXbrack, TeXproj, TeXaligned, TeXreplace, NoDollars are global variables used to control LaTeX typesetting of Singular objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TeXwidth (int) controls breaking of long polynomials: -1, 0, 1..9, >9. TeXnofrac (int flag) makes fractions print as '1/2' instead of \frac{1}{2}. TeXbrack (string) sets brackets around ideals/matrices (e.g. "{", "(", "<", "|", or empty). TeXproj (int flag) prints ":" instead of "," in vectors. TeXaligned (int flag) makes maps/ideals aligned. TeXreplace is a list of 2-string entries for symbol replacement (e.g. replace "@phi" by "\\phi"). NoDollars (int flag) suppresses surrounding $ signs. Use texdemo() to generate texlibdemo.tex explaining full features and interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: closetex(fname)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writes a LaTeX2e closing line into file <fname>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: closetex(fname); fname is string. Preceding '>>' in fname are removed and '.tex' is appended if missing. Returns nothing. Example sequence: LIB "latex.lib"; opentex("exmpl"); texobj(...); closetex("exmpl");

rubrics_metrics.name: opentex(fname)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writes a LaTeX2e header into a new file <fname> (starts a .tex file).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: opentex(fname); fname string. Removes preceding '>>' and appends '.tex' if not given. Returns nothing. Example: opentex("exmpl"); texobj("exmpl","hello"); closetex("exmpl");

rubrics_metrics.name: tex(fname)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls the LaTeX2e engine to compile the file fname (.tex).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: tex(fname); fname string. Leading '>>' removed and '.tex' appended if missing. The procedure invokes system latex and writes .dvi/.log output; examples in the manual show typical latex log lines. Returns nothing; examples demonstrate the creation of exp001.dvi and exp001.log. Note: environment must have latex installed and available.

rubrics_metrics.name: texdemo()
rubrics_metrics.description: Generates a demonstration LaTeX file (texlibdemo.tex) explaining latex.lib features and global variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: texdemo(); returns nothing and generates texlibdemo.tex to show examples of the library features (recommended to learn default formatting behavior).

rubrics_metrics.name: texfactorize(fname,f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Produces LaTeX typesetting of the factorization of polynomial f or writes it into file <fname>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: texfactorize(fname,f); if fname=="" returns a string with f factorized in TeX form; otherwise appends that string to <fname>. Preceding '>>' in fname are removed and '.tex' appended if missing. Examples show factorization results and behavior on different coefficient rings (integers mod p, algebraic extensions).

rubrics_metrics.name: texmap(fname,m,@r1,@r2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typeset a ring map m from ring @r1 to ring @r2 in TeX; either return a string or append to a file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: texmap("", "@phi", @r1, r2) returns TeX string; with non-empty fname appends to file. Preceding '>>' removed and '.tex' appended. If m is a string it must be the name of an existing map. Example demonstrates mapping phi:\Q[x,y,z] -> \Q[u,v] and use of TeXreplace to substitute '@phi'→'\\phi'. TeXaligned influences alignment; TeXbrack influences delimiters.

rubrics_metrics.name: texname(fname,s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforms an arbitrary string s into a TeX-safe name according to specific character rules and returns or appends it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: texname("", s) returns transformed string. Rules include handling of tildes (s' + "~" → \\tilde{...}), underscores with integers produce subscripts, uppercase letters with integers become superscripts, bracketed expressions drop outer braces, parentheses containing (int, s') map to combined sub/superscript form, etc. If fname provided, transformed string is appended to file. Examples: texname("","f(10)") → f(10); texname("","f23") → f_{23}; texname("","E~(3)") → \tilde{E}_{3}.

rubrics_metrics.name: texobj(fname,l)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typesets entries of a Singular list l in LaTeX: supports polynomials, ideals, matrices, integer matrices and lists; returns string or appends to file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: texobj(fname,l); if fname=="" returns TeX string. Preceding '>>' removed and '.tex' appended. Examples: polynomials printed in display math arrays; ideals printed as parenthesized lists; TeXaligned, TeXbrack control alignment and delimiter style; matrices printed with appropriate column alignment; intmats printed with right-justified columns. Use examples to see formatting of polynomials, ideals (jacobian), matrices, and intmats. Restore global variables if previously defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: texpoly(fname,p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Produces a TeX representation of polynomial p or appends it to file <fname>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: texpoly(fname,p); if fname=="" returns TeX string. Preceding '>>' removed and '.tex' appended. Handles different base rings: real, rational, finite prime fields, algebraic extensions; formats floating coefficients (e.g. 2.000x^{2}...) and rational coefficients as \frac when appropriate unless TeXnofrac set. Examples illustrate formatting across rings (real, prime fields, algebraic extension parameters).

rubrics_metrics.name: texproc(fname,pname)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs the source of a Singular procedure pname in a LaTeX verbatim environment, either returning the string or appending it to <fname>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: texproc(fname,pname); pname must be a defined procedure. If the procedure isn't found prints an error. Preceding '>>' removed and '.tex' appended. The function collects parameter and alias lines, slices procedure body between return markers and wraps in \begin{verbatim}...\end{verbatim}. Example: texproc("","texproc") returns the textual representation of proc texproc. If fname=="" returns the string; otherwise writes to file.

rubrics_metrics.name: texring(fname, r[,L])
rubrics_metrics.description: Generates TeX-typesetting for a ring r; optional list L controls additional formatting (e.g., symbol for coefficient field).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: texring(fname, r[, L]); if fname=="" returns TeX string. Removes '>>' and appends '.tex'. Examples show output for polynomial rings over Q, power series rings, finite fields (\F_{49}[x]), quotient rings (\Q[x,y]/(y^3-x^2)), algebraic extensions with parameter names, local vs polynomial orderings, and options to print truncated variable lists (x_0,...,x_9). The optional L may specify display choices like 'mipo' for minpoly display.

rubrics_metrics.name: rmx(fname)
rubrics_metrics.description: Removes auxiliary LaTeX files (.log, .aux) associated with <fname>; optionally .dvi or .tex if fname ends with those suffixes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: rmx(fname); fname string. Removes associated files created by tex() for cleanup. Example: after tex("exp001") call rmx("exp001") to remove exp001.* files. Preceding '>>' removed and '.tex' appended if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: xdvi(fname[,style])
rubrics_metrics.description: Displays the .dvi file fname.dvi in the xdvi previewer (or alternative specified by style).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: xdvi(fname[,style]); suffix .dvi may be omitted. 'style' if given selects another program instead of default xdvi. Example sequences show compiling to .dvi via tex() and then calling xdvi("exp001") which invokes the previewer. Requires xdvi (or provided previewer) installed.

rubrics_metrics.name: plot(I) (surf.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot procedure that visualizes plane curves or surfaces defined by a polynomial/ideal using external 'surf' program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: plot(I); I is an ideal or polynomial defining a plane curve or a surface by one equation. Requires external program 'surf' installed. To close the graphical interface press 'Q'. Examples include plotting plane curves, Steiner surface, Whitney umbrella, and algebraic curve logos. Returns nothing; depends on having 'surf' available and in path.

rubrics_metrics.name: surfer(f) (surf.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opens the external program 'surfer' to visualize the surface defined by polynomial f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: surfer(f); f poly (one equation). Requires 'surfer' installed (version requirement noted). Close the surfer window to exit. Examples: calling surfer on standard surfaces (Whitney umbrella, E7).

rubrics_metrics.name: plotRotated(poly p, list coords, list #) (surfex.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses surfex to draw a surface p in the real affine space with coordinates coords; optional int parameter controls plotting quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: plotRotated(p, list(x,y,z), quality?). coords must be a list of three variables. Base ring must have characteristic zero and no parameters. Opens surfex external program. Example: plotRotated(cayley_cubic, list(x,y,z)); optional quality setting increases render quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotRot(poly p, list #) (surfex.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar to plotRotated but guesses which coordinates to use automatically; optional int parameter adjusts plotting quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: plotRot(p, quality?). Works when polynomial uses exactly three variables or when polynomial is embedded in ring with more vars. Base ring must be characteristic zero without parameters. Additional parameter (e.g., 3) can request Singular to compute singular locus prior to calling surfex for tricky surfaces (examples: solitary points, swallowtail).

rubrics_metrics.name: plotRotatedList(list varieties, list coords, list #) (surfex.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Draws multiple surfaces/varieties with surfex using given coordinates; varieties is a list of ideals describing each variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: plotRotatedList(list(cayley_cubic, plane), list(x,y,z)); optional int parameter sets plotting quality. Example demonstrates showing cubic surface together with a tritangent plane and variants where plane is provided as ideal for intersection-only display.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotRotatedDirect(list varieties, list #) (surfex.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sends equations directly to surfex, expecting variable names x,y,z; supports passing parameters p1,p2,... to surfex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: plotRotatedDirect(list(varieties), quality?). The 'varieties' list format is less documented; examples show how to pass polynomials or strings representing surfex-readable polynomials, and specify rendering parameters (camera, frames, expressions depending on parameters). Advantage: supports parameters p1,p2 that will be passed to surfex. Ensure variable names are x,y,z when using this direct mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotRotatedListFromSpecifyList(list varietiesList, list #) (surfex.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced plotting entry that accepts a complex specification list (varietiesList) for surfex; optional quality parameter available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: plotRotatedListFromSpecifyList(varietiesList, quality?). The format for varietiesList is complicated and not fully documented; examples in the manual should be adapted. Base ring must be characteristic zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: brnoeth.lib intended domain
rubrics_metrics.description: Brnoeth library implements Brill–Noether algorithm, Weierstrass semigroups and AG-code utilities intended only for plane (possibly singular) curves defined over a prime field of positive characteristic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: procedures assume the curve is a plane curve over a prime field of positive characteristic; consult the brnoeth.lib header for additional implementation details and constraints. Using it outside that domain may yield incorrect results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adj_div(f[,l]) (brnoeth.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes and stores fundamental data of the plane curve defined by f needed for AG codes; returns a structured list L with rings, degree/genus, closed places, conductor, and local-ring data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: Adj_div(f) or Adj_div(f,l). Returns list L where L[1] contains affine and projective rings, L[2] is intvec (degree, genus), L[3] list of intvecs for closed places, L[4] conductor intvec, L[5] local-ring data organized by extension degree. Affine ring contains CHI (affine equation), Aff_SLocus (affine singular locus), Inf Points, Aff_SPoints, etc. Conductor computed by local invariants by default; can be computed by Dedekind formula with optional args. printlevel controls verbosity (default 0). Warning: field extension parameter is named 'a' so no global object named 'a' should exist when running Adj_div. Example sequences show how to inspect returned structures and switch rings for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSplaces(h, CURVE) (brnoeth.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes all non-singular affine closed places whose degrees are in the intvec h and updates the CURVE data list produced by Adj_div.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: NSplaces(h, C) where h is an intvec of degrees and C is the output of Adj_div. Returns updated list L with new entries: in L[1][1] affine ring contains Aff_Points(d) lists for each degree d; in L[3] closed places updated; L[5] local rings created/updated for new places. printlevel increases verbosity. Warning: the field-extension parameter is 'a' and must not clash with a global object named 'a'. Examples show creating places up to degree 4 and examining Aff_Points and local rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: BrillNoether(G, CURVE) (brnoeth.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes a vector-space basis of the Riemann–Roch space L(G) for rational divisor G on a non-singular curve; returns a list of ideals representing numerator/denominator pairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: BrillNoether(G, CURVE) where G is an intvec representing the rational divisor supported on CURVE[3]. Must be called from ring CURVE[1][2] (the projective ring). Returns list of ideals (each with two homogeneous generators representing numerator and denominator). Example: compute basis for G = 4*C[3][1]+4*C[3][3] after preparing curve with Adj_div and NSplaces; success message 'Vector basis successfully computed' displayed. Inspect output to get rational function generators for L(G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weierstrass(i, m, CURVE) (brnoeth.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the Weierstrass semigroup at place i up to integer m and returns associated rational functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: Weierstrass(i, m, CURVE). Must be called from ring CURVE[1][2]. Returns WS where WS[1] is list of integers (Weierstrass semigroup up to m) and WS[2] is list of ideals representing the associated rational functions (numerator/denominator pairs). Warning: the place must be rational (i.e., CURVE[3][i][1] == 1). Examples and further notes are provided in the brnoeth section.
